title: About

title: Custom Instrumentation for Chiroptical Spectroscopy
content: A 3D-printed sample fixture for the CD spectrometer, designed in Fusion 360, and the chiral metasurface signal it made reproducible. Shadi Mirmohammadi, Tang Lab, University of Utah. 01 The problem 02 The fixture 03 The measurement 04 Credits 01 The problem Circular dichroism (CD) is the difference in absorption between left- and right-circularly polarized light. For a chiral metasurface the signal is a few millidegrees riding on a much larger absorbance, so the position of the substrate in the beam matters: hand-placing a coated fused-silica chip in the sample compartment shifts and reshapes the spectrum from scan to scan. Moving the chip from mid-beam toward the detector weakens and shifts the couplet: the positive lobe goes from +14.3 to +11.2 mdeg. Side view of the sample compartment. Placed by hand, the chip can sit anywhere along the beam between the source and the detector; the rail mount and holder seat it at one position. The beam path with the chip placed by hand at two positions, then seated by the rail mount and holder; the holder is also shown from the front. 02 The fixture I designed a two-part fixture in Fusion 360 and 3D-printed it. A rail mount slides into the Jasco spectrometer's sample compartment at a fixed position along the beam path, and a square substrate holder seats the chip at the same position and orientation every time. Two printed parts; the holder took six design iterations. The holder has a recessed pocket for the chip and corner mounting holes. The figure shows the Fusion 360 models of both parts. title: Electrochemical Sol-Gelation of CdS Quantum Dots
content: Growing 3D quantum-dot gel networks under applied potential: phase- and size-dependent electrogelation of CdS QDs. Shadi Mirmohammadi, Department of Chemistry, University of Utah, with the Luo lab; SAXS at the Utah Nanofab with Randy Polson. 01 Gels grown by voltage 02 How it works 03 The dots 04 Growth at three potentials 05 Structure by SAXS 06 Credits 01 Gels grown by voltage Zinc-blende CdS quantum dots capped with thioglycolic acid link into a three-dimensional network on a platinum anode when a potential is applied. The gel grows on the electrode itself, without a chemical oxidant. Gels grow at 1.7 to 1.9 V vs Ag/AgCl. The video is the 1.8 V cell, 36 µM CdS@TGA in methanol, with the gel nucleating on the Pt anode. Gelation cross-links the dots into a continuous, porous 3D network that keeps quantum confinement while allowing electronic communication. Most QD gels are made by adding a chemical oxidant, which leaves residue and gives uncontrolled nucleation. Your browser does not support the video tag. 1.8 V vs. Ag/AgCl · 36 µM CdS@TGA in methanol · gel nucleating on the Pt anode 02 How it works Anodic oxidation of the surface thiolates forms S₂²⁻ bridges between neighbouring dots, so the network grows directly on the electrode and the applied potential sets the oxidation strength. Scanning from 1.4 to 2.4 V shows a sharp onset: below ~1.6 V nothing happens, and from ~1.7 V a translucent yellow gel nucleates and grows around the anode, with controlled kinetics and no chemical oxidant. title: Photon Upconversion in CdSe–Anthracene Hybrids
content: CdSe nanoplatelet–anthracene hybrids that convert two green photons into one violet photon, and how the position of one carboxylic acid on the anthracene sets the upconversion yield. Seyedeh Shadi Mirmohammadi, Farwa Awan, Tsumugi Miyashita, Todd D. Krauss, and Ming Lee Tang, University of Utah & University of Rochester.Poster presented at the 2nd International Symposium on Photochemistry & Functional Interfaces (ISPF2), New York, 2024. Poster 01 The relay 02 Nanoplatelets and three isomers 03 Measured yields 04 Transient absorption 05 Poster and support 01 The relay Two green photons become one violet photon through triplet–triplet annihilation (TTA). A CdSe nanoplatelet absorbs the 532 nm light, an anthracenecarboxylic acid (ACA) bound to its surface takes the triplet by Dexter transfer, and a free emitter in solution, 9,10-diphenylanthracene (DPA), collects it and emits at 410 nm. 2.34 eV in at 532 nm, 3.06 eV out at 410 nm. The triplet steps down from the platelet to ACA at 1.83 eV and on to DPA at 1.77 eV; when two DPA triplets meet, TTA lifts one to the emitting singlet. Two Dexter steps, TET1 to the mediator and TET2 to the emitter, then TTA. In this work the Tang lab's CdSe quantum dots were replaced with nanoplatelets. The energy ladder of the relay: 532 nm absorption in the nanoplatelet, two Dexter triplet transfers (TET1, TET2), triplet–triplet annihilation (TTA) and 410 nm emission from DPA. title: EIT-Like Terahertz Metasurface: a Full-Wave Design Study
content: A published EIT terahertz metasurface reproduced and extended in Ansys HFSS, covering metal thickness relative to the skin depth, substrate selection, and a coupled-resonator fit to the full-wave data. Shadi Mirmohammadi, ECE 6310 (Advanced Electromagnetic Fields), University of Utah, Spring 2026.Course project (instructor: Prof. Berardi Sensale-Rodriguez); reproduces and extends Zhang et al. [1]. ReportExplorer 01 The transparency window 02 Validation 03 Interactive explorer 04 Mode switching 05 The sweeps 06 Report and talk 01 The transparency window Two coupled resonators whose responses interfere destructively open a narrow transparency window between two absorption dips, the metamaterial counterpart of electromagnetically induced transparency. I rebuilt the aluminum C-arc and S-arc cell of Zhang et al. [1] in Ansys HFSS to reproduce the window, then asked two fabrication questions the paper did not address. A single resonator has one broad dip. The coupled cell transmits again through a window at 0.81 THz, where the steep phase gives a peak group delay of 5.3 ps. Floquet-port excitation, periodic boundaries, ΔS < 0.02 convergence. Dashed: a single resonator alone; blue: the coupled cell; red: the group delay from the exported S-parameters. The cell and its simulated transmission, 0.5 to 1.4 THz: single resonator (dashed), coupled cell (blue), group delay (red) peaking at 5.3 ps in the window. 02 Validation Before changing anything I checked the model against the published device, feature by feature. title: 10 kV β-Ga₂O₃ Photoconductive Switches
content: Impurity-engineered Fe:β-Ga₂O₃ photoconductive semiconductor switches that switch 10 kV with a near-infrared laser. Hunter Ellis, Imteaz Rahaman, Afrouz Taherian, Seyedeh Shadi Mirmohammadi, Botong Li, Michael A. Scarpulla, Berardi Sensale-Rodriguez, and Kai Fu, Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering, University of Utah.Manuscript ready for submission (2026). The work was led by Hunter Ellis in the Fu group. Related 01 Sub-bandgap trigger 02 The switch and the bench 03 Measured photocurrent 04 What the data say 05 Paper and related work 01 Sub-bandgap trigger β-Ga2O3 holds off high voltage because its bandgap is wide, but band-to-band absorption needs deep-ultraviolet light, and fast high-power UV sources are scarce. Fe doping adds a deep acceptor level that an ordinary 808 nm near-infrared laser can ionize, so the switch keeps its full blocking capability and needs no UV source. The Fe level sits about 0.8 eV below the conduction band of the 4.8 eV gap; an 808 nm photon carries 1.53 eV, enough to lift an electron from the Fe level into the conduction band. Shallow impurity levels give optical access with inexpensive near-infrared lasers at the cost of thermal stability; the deeper mid-gap levels drawn for comparison (Co, Ir, Ni, Cu) promise stability but need higher photon energies. Band diagram of Fe:β-Ga₂O₃: an 808 nm photon (1.53 eV) lifts an electron from the Fe level, 0.8 eV below the conduction band, across the 4.8 eV gap. Other transition-metal levels are drawn for comparison. 02 The switch and the bench The switch is a pair of Ti/Au contacts on an F...

title: Excitation-Switchable Eu³⁺ Luminescence in GdScO₃
content: A nominally undoped crystal changes its emission color with the excitation wavelength, and its luminescence reports on substrate quality. Seyedeh Shadi Mirmohammadi, Afrouz Taherian, Yunshan Wang, Diego P. Fernandez, Michael A. Scarpulla, Steve Blair, and Berardi Sensale-Rodriguez, University of Utah.Manuscript in preparation for Optical Materials Express (2026). Poster accepted at MRS Fall 2026, Symposium EL03. PL explorerTransmission explorer 01 Trace Eu in undoped GdScO₃ 02 The excitation switch 03 Interactive dataset 04 Identifying the emitter 05 Annealing at 1200 °C 06 Manuscript and data 01 Trace Eu in undoped GdScO₃ GdScO₃ is a perovskite substrate for epitaxial oxide films. Commercial, nominally undoped single crystals from two vendors show bright, sharp visible emission under deep-UV excitation, and the emitter is europium at the parts-per-million level. Eu³⁺ at 1–2 ppm, roughly one Eu³⁺ ion per 10⁵–10⁶ Gd³⁺. The trace emits strongly because energy absorbed anywhere in the Gd³⁺ sublattice migrates to the Eu³⁺ sites. Crystals: Stonylab (100) and CrysTec (110). Each row of the map is one emission spectrum from the excitation sweep, normalized per excitation; the lines are the Eu³⁺ ⁵D₂ (491 nm) and ⁵D₀ (590 and 612 nm) transitions. title: UV Photoresponsivity of GeO₂ Photodetectors
content: Measuring the deep-UV spectral response of ultrawide-bandgap GeO₂ detectors with a tunable third-harmonic laser source, in collaboration with the Fu and Blair labs. Shadi Mirmohammadi, with Imteaz Rahaman, Botong Li, and Afrouz Taherian (Dr. Kai Fu's lab) and Prof. Steve Blair, Electrical & Computer Engineering, University of Utah.Manuscript in preparation. Fu lab 01 Solar-blind detectors 02 Measured responsivity 03 Switching 04 Roles and manuscript 01 Solar-blind detectors Germanium dioxide is an emerging ultrawide-bandgap semiconductor, and a detector built on it responds only in the solar-blind ultraviolet, where sunlight does not reach the ground. Dr. Kai Fu's group fabricated metal–semiconductor–metal detectors on their GeO2 films, and the quantitative test is how the responsivity varies with wavelength across the band edge. Rutile r-GeO2(111) grown by MOCVD on r-TiO2(111), optical bandgap ~5.31 eV; interdigitated contacts with a 250 × 300 µm active area; tunable light at ~233 to 280 nm from third-harmonic generation of a Ti:sapphire laser. The source is my UV-pumped photoluminescence setup in Prof. Blair's lab, realigned for this experiment; I calibrated the power at each wavelength on a Thorlabs power meter with a UV extension. Responsivity is (Iphoto − Idark) / Pincident from dual-sweep I–V curves between −10 and +10 V in the dark and under illumination. The beam is ~7 mm across and the device 250 × 300 µm, so the incident power is corrected by the beam-to-device area ratio of 512.87. title: Optical Constants of 3D-Printable Glass on Doped SiC
content: Spectroscopic ellipsometry of Glassomer films on doped silicon carbide, with Cauchy and oscillator modeling of Ψ and Δ and validation against literature optical constants. Shadi Mirmohammadi, Electrical & Computer Engineering, University of Utah 01 Why ellipsometry 02 Calibration 03 Modeling 04 Literature check 05 Notes 01 Why ellipsometry Designing a photonic device around a material requires its refractive index, n and k, across the wavelengths of interest. Spectroscopic ellipsometry measures the polarization change on reflection as the angles Ψ and Δ, and the optical constants come from fitting a physical model to them. The material is Glassomer, a 3D-printable silica-nanopowder-filled composite debound and sintered into fused silica, on doped silicon carbide. Five stacks were measured: two Glassomer films on doped SiC, one SiC / Glassomer / SiC sandwich and two bare doped SiC references. Ψ and Δ were recorded from 250 to 2000 nm at 60°, 65°, 70°, and 75° incidence. The 1750 to 2000 nm region was noisy at the edge of the detector range, so the working window was tightened to 250 to 1750 nm. title: Engineering Spin States in Si QD–Organic Hybrids
content: Time-resolved EPR shows that Si quantum dots transfer a fully spin-polarized triplet to covalently bound anthracene derivatives. Mandefro Y. Teferi, Sanoop Mambully Somasundaran, Shadi Mirmohammadi, Ming Lee Tang, Jens Niklas, and Oleg G. Poluektov. Argonne National Laboratory & Department of Chemistry, University of Utah.Nano Letters (2026), doi: 10.1021/acs.nanolett.6c03633. Accepted September 10, 2026. Poster at ESP-2025, Best Poster Award. PaperPoster 01 Why TR-EPR 02 The emissive spectrum 03 Linker and delocalization 04 Paper, poster and support 01 Why TR-EPR Si quantum dot–molecule hybrids generate long-lived triplet excitons, but nearly everything known about their triplet energy transfer comes from optical measurements, which do not resolve spin. Time-resolved electron paramagnetic resonance (TR-EPR) does: it can tell a triplet formed by spin–orbit intersystem crossing from one formed by charge recombination or direct energy transfer. The conjugates pair 2.6 nm dodecane-capped Si QDs with three anthracene derivatives covalently bound through different bridges. The 480 nm excitation is absorbed only by the QD, so any triplet on the molecule came from the dot. 9-ethylanthracene (9EA, flexible single bond), 9-vinylanthracene (9VA, π-conjugated C=C linker) and the larger 9,10-bis(phenylethynyl)anthracene (BPEA). title: Optically Tunable THz Metasurface Absorber
content: An optically tunable terahertz metasurface absorber on Fe-doped β-Ga₂O₃: HFSS design, measured photoconductivity, the ITO electrode process, and the first resonator array on the crystal. Poster at IRMMW-THz 2026. Seyedeh Shadi Mirmohammadi, Steve Blair and Berardi Sensale-Rodriguez, University of Utah.IRMMW-THz 2026, Salt Lake City. Poster: Monday October 12, 17:30 to 19:00, Poster Session 1, Board 1. PosterCodeExplorer 01 The idea 02 Simulated switching 03 Measured photoconductivity 04 The fabricated array 05 The ITO electrode 06 Paper, poster and code 01 The idea Fe-doped β-Ga2O3 is an ultrawide-bandgap crystal that an 808 nm laser can make conductive through its Fe acceptor states. Put a resonator array on it and the pump tunes the whole array, with no contacts, gates or heaters. The Fe level sits about 0.85 eV below the conduction band; the published photoconductivity reaches ~25 S/m at 2 W of 808 nm light [1]. Unit cell: a gold H-shaped resonator (P 150, a 120, w 15, g 5 µm, 0.2 µm Au) on 724 µm of Fe:β-Ga₂O₃ over a gold ground plane.
